ai.description: *Gerrhopilus tindalli* is a slender, worm-like snake reaching 15–20 cm. It is uniform dark brown with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include 20 midbody scale rows and 260–270 ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gerrhopilus tindalli* is best distinguished by its unique scale arrangement, specifically possessing 14 rows of scales around the midbody, unlike most similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: Tindall's Worm Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in leaf litter at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Tindall's worm snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours burrowing through leaf litter and soil in search of small invertebrate prey like ant larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gerrhopilus tindalli* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding details remain limited, it is believed to reproduce during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Gerrhopilus tindalli is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the high-elevation forests of the Nilgiris and Anaimalai hills.
